nv-leg-2026-senate-members.title: Senate: current members, with district, party, counties and Term Ends
nv-leg-2026-senate-members.note: Which Senate seats are on the 2026 ballot: the 11 whose Term Ends year is 2026 (districts 2, 8, 9, 10, 12, 13, 14, 16, 17, 20, 21), and the counties each district reaches. Only each member row's name, party, district and county cells and the Term Ends field are read; the page's contact details are never read or kept.

nv-leg-2026-assembly-members.title: Assembly: current members, with district, party, counties and Term Ends
nv-leg-2026-assembly-members.note: Every Assembly term ends in 2026 (42 of 42 as read). Only name, party, district, county and Term Ends are read.

nv-leg-constitution-art5.title: Constitution of the State of Nevada, Article 5, Sections 2, 17 and 19
nv-leg-constitution-art5.note: The governor is elected every four years at the legislative elections; the lieutenant governor, secretary of state, treasurer, controller and attorney general at the same time. Each section's words checked on the page: Section 2 found, Section 17 found, Section 19 found.

nv-openstates-roster.title: Sitting legislators and statewide officials
nv-openstates-roster.note: Who holds each seat today (ids, names, parties, districts and term ends only); it does not carry the Treasurer, the Controller or judges.

nv-census-2024-county-codes.title: Cartographic boundary file, counties, 2024 (1:500,000)
nv-census-2024-county-codes.note: Five-digit county codes for the counties the Legislature lists under each district, and the names of Nevada's seventeen counties (Carson City among them) for the county pages.

nv-clark-2026-general-contests.title: All Contests and Candidates in the November 3, 2026, General Election in Clark County, Nevada
nv-clark-2026-general-contests.note: Clark County's own list of every contest and candidate on its November ballot. A ruled table of five columns, read by its own lines: contest, name on the ballot (last name; first, middle or nickname), party and term. Read twice, by the ruled lines and again line by line, and the two readings agree. The file has no address, telephone, e-mail or website column of any kind, so nothing of that sort is read or kept. 254 names in all: 148 in 89 county, township, city, school, district and local court contests are loaded; 106 in 53 federal and state contests (Congress, the statewide offices, the Legislature, the Supreme Court and the Board of Regents) are left to the state's own list; 8 lines reading None of these candidates are not candidates. The list says it is in order of appearance on the ballot, subject to change, and that order is stored. It has no status column: a candidate who withdrew is simply not on it.

nv-washoe-2026-general-contests.title: Washoe County 2026 General Election Contests (workbook)
nv-washoe-2026-general-contests.note: Washoe County's own list of every contest and candidate on its November ballot. A workbook of one sheet, its columns found by their headings: Name on Ballot, Party, Office Sought, Office Type, Term Length and Vote For. Read twice, through a workbook reader and again from the workbook's own XML, and the two readings agree. The file has no address, telephone, e-mail or website column of any kind, so nothing of that sort is read or kept. 103 names in all: 60 in 36 county, township, city, school, district and local court contests are loaded; 43 in 21 federal and state contests (Congress, the statewide offices, the Legislature, the Supreme Court and the Board of Regents) are left to the state's own list; 8 lines reading None of these candidates are not candidates; 3 ballot questions in the table below the candidates are not read. The list states no ballot order, so none is stored. It has no status column: a candidate who withdrew is simply not on it.

nv-census-2020-places.title: 2020 place codes, Nevada (st32_nv_place2020.txt)
nv-census-2020-places.note: The code and the name of each incorporated city on the counties' lists (7 used here): Henderson city, Reno city and so on. Places only; the file names no person.

local_calendar.t: Nevada holds its general election in November of each even-numbered year, and county, township, city, school district and general improvement district offices are filled at it, so those whose terms are ending are on the November 3, 2026 ballot. A nonpartisan office is missing from it when the June 9 primary settled it: a candidate with no opponent, or one who won a majority there, was declared elected (a judge of the district court in that position goes on to November alone). Irrigation districts hold their own elections in April.

local_coverage.t: Loaded for two of Nevada's seventeen counties, Clark and Washoe, each from its own election office's list of November contests and candidates: 125 contests and 208 names (county offices and constables; district court judges, justices of the peace and municipal court judges; city offices; school district trustees; water, improvement and other district boards). The other fifteen counties are not loaded yet. Not loaded from these lists: ballot questions, and the federal and state offices they also carry (Congress, the statewide offices, the Legislature, the Supreme Court and the Board of Regents). An office settled at the June primary is on neither list, because it is not on the November ballot.
local_coverage.s: Clark County Election Department and Washoe County Registrar of Voters: each county's own list of November 3, 2026 contests and candidates
